about: Fourth, labelled attack list: test gaps found by mutation testing on contract v2 (app/contracts/mutants.test.mjs, first run 2026-11-20 20:03 IST). Deleting `require(this.activeInputIndex == 0)` from any path left every earlier attack refused, so no test proved that check matters. These attacks would get through without it. Written before any run of this list; lists 1-3 are unchanged. Every attack must be rejected.

attacks.what: steal the shop's minting token: put the minter at input 1 behind the attacker's own coin at input 0, and send output 0 (the minting token) to the attacker's address, which matches input 0
with the stolen hot refund key: minter at input 1, attacker's coin at input 0, and the minting token plus the whole float sent to the attacker at output 0
with the stolen hot refund key: the same input-order trick through the partial-refund path
use the owner's admin path without the owner's key (signed by the hot refund key) to take the float

with the stolen hot refund key: the attacker's own token category's minting token at input 0, the minter at input 1 and a fake receipt in the attacker's category at input 2, so the refund path reads the attacker's category; the shop's minting token and float go to the attacker
attacks.added: 2026-11-20 20:12 IST after the first mutation run with K01-K04: deleting the input-order check from refund and partialRefund still survived, and checking each survivor by hand showed this attack gets through without it

attacks.what: the same attacker-category trick through the partial-refund path
